limitations_and_boundaries: The in vivo study showed a trend of synergy between YAP knockdown and lapatinib but was not statistically significant; more comprehensive animal studies are required.
Compensatory activation of HER3 was not strongly observed under the conditions tested (1.5 μM lapatinib, 48 h), but may occur at lower concentrations or later time points.
The study focused on a single HER2-amplified cell line (HCC1569) for most experiments; generalizability to other HER2+ breast cancers is not established.
The role of other microenvironmental factors beyond rigidity (e.g., biochemical composition) was not fully dissected.
YAP and TAZ may have distinct functions in vivo, but in vitro knockdown of either eliminated modulus-dependent resistance, suggesting redundancy in this context.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

provenance.text_excerpt: Thus HCC1569 cells responded to lapatinib in an elastic modulus–dependent manner, showing greater resistance to the antiproliferative effect of lapatinib on rigid matrices.

experiments_or_tasks: HCC1569 and BT549 cells were cultured on 400-Pa PA gels or TCP coated with type 1 collagen for 48 h, then treated with 1.5 μM lapatinib or DMSO for 48 h. EdU incorporation was measured. IC50 was determined from dose-response curves.

methods.protocol_description: Cells were cultured on PA gels of 400 ± 160 Pa or TCP coated with type 1 collagen for 48 h, then treated with lapatinib or DMSO for 48 h. EdU incorporation was measured. IC50 was calculated from dose-response curves.

provenance.text_excerpt: The half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of lapatinib was threefold lower on 400-Pa PA gels than with TCP, 0.9 and 2.7 μM, respectively (Figure 1E).

HCC1569 cells were more sensitive to lapatinib on 400-Pa PA gels than on TCP coated with type 1 collagen, with 50 ± 4.5 and 69 ± 4.5% EdU incorporation, respectively (Figure 1, C and D); BT549 cells were not affected by lapatinib or changes in rigidity (Figure 1, C and D).

research_questions.statement: Does YAP knockdown in vivo increase sensitivity to lapatinib?

provenance.text_excerpt: These data demonstrate that YAP knockdown was sufficient to reduce growth of HER2-amplified cell lines in vivo, and they suggest that YAP knockdown and lapatinib together may have some synergistic benefit.

experiments_or_tasks: HCC1569 cells with IPTG-inducible YAP shRNA were implanted in mice. Tumor volume was measured over 23 days in four groups: no IPTG/no lapatinib (A), IPTG only (B), lapatinib only (C), lapatinib + IPTG (D).

methods.name: Xenograft tumor model with IPTG-inducible shRNA
methods.protocol_description: HCC1569 cells with IPTG-inducible YAP shRNA were implanted in mice. Mice were treated with or without IPTG and lapatinib. Tumor volume was measured over time.

study_units.name: YAP knockdown in vivo with lapatinib treatment

provenance.text_excerpt: Mice that received neither IPTG nor lapatinib (group A) had the maximum tumor volume (mean of volume, 1280 mm3) by day 23. Mice treated with IPTG (group B) had significantly decreased (p < 0.05) tumor volume (mean of volume, 770 mm3) compared with group A. Lapatinib treatment groups either with (group D) or without IPTG treatment (group C) had much smaller tumor volumes compared with groups A and B. Group D, which received lapatinib and had reduced YAP levels, had the smallest tumor volumes (mean of volume, 192 mm3), even compared with group C (mean of volume, 269 mm3); however, that difference was not statistically significant.

results.value_raw_text: Group A: 1280 mm³; Group B: 770 mm³ (p<0.05 vs A); Group C: 269 mm³; Group D: 192 mm³ (not significant vs C)
